text: If the city allows a single high-rise apartment building in our residential neighborhood, it sets a precedent. Developers will see that the zoning board is willing to make exceptions, and within a few years, we'll have a corridor of towers where single-family homes used to be. I've seen it happen in other neighborhoods. Once you open that door, it's very hard to close it again.

metadata.note: Precedent-based reasoning is legitimate in legal and zoning contexts — precedent genuinely does influence future decisions. The speaker's chain of causation (one exception leads to many) is plausible rather than fantastical. This is borderline between a valid concern about institutional precedent and a slippery slope fallacy.
